stated_request: Is there any way for the system to put claims into a pile automatically? My team spends the first hour of every shift just sorting.
Claims sit in unsorted because we can't decide until the police reference comes in. Can we park them somewhere so they stop showing as overdue?
After the hailstorm on 9 May we had 1,140 new claims in two days against a normal 300. The unsorted queue hit 26 hours. We need help with surges.
The sort screen takes 6 to 8 seconds to load claim history. It slows everything down.
Two handlers put identical windscreen claims in different piles. We need sorting to be consistent.
A customer submitted four claims for the same incident by mistake and we paid two of them. The sort screen doesn't show related claims.
We wait on photos from the customer for most motor claims, about two days on average. Sorting isn't the slow bit, getting the information is.
Please add auto-sorting. Our board is asking why we still do this by hand.
The suspicious pile needs a supervisor to approve before it goes to investigation. The supervisor is often in meetings, so claims wait hours.
Our auditor asked why a claim was marked simple. Keelwater records who sorted it, but not why.
Glass-only claims under £300 are always simple. Can we select a load of them and sort them in one go?
Lots of claims arrive without a policy number. Handlers can't sort without it and have to look it up in another system.
Our own report says we moved 6% of last month's claims to a different pile after the first week. Most went from simple to needs a closer look once the engineer's report arrived.
The pile dropdown resets if you open the attachments tab. I lost my selection three times today.
Can Keelwater recommend a pile? We don't want it decided for us, but a starting point would help new starters.
Storm again: 900 claims in and half the team on leave. Is there anything that can tell us which unsorted claims to look at first?
Third-party claims wait for the other insurer to confirm liability before we can tell if they're simple. Usually one to three days.
Auto-sorting please. The competitor's product does it now.
New handlers send far too many claims to suspicious, which clogs investigation. Experienced handlers almost never do.
We'd love bulk sorting for the simple ones. Selecting them one by one is painful on Monday mornings.
Linked claims, like the driver and a passenger from the same accident, come in separately and get sorted by different people. One went simple, one went suspicious.
If you add any automatic sorting, we'll need to show the regulator exactly why each claim went where it did.
Is auto-sort on the roadmap? Asking for our ops director.
Waiting on the repair estimate from the garage is our biggest delay. Claims sit unsorted for a day or more.
From our export: of 4,200 claims in July, 610 took more than four hours to sort. Nearly all of those were waiting on something from the customer.
Our sorting backlog after a weekend is 400 to 600 claims. Monday mornings are spent catching up.
Search on the sort screen doesn't find claims by vehicle registration.
Investigation sent back 22% of what we referred last quarter as not suspicious. We need better guidance on what goes in the suspicious pile.
Can we auto-sort the claims that clearly don't need a human, like low-value glass?
Large-loss claims need a manager to sign off the pile. Our managers cover two sites, so it can take half a day.
When a claim is moved to a different pile later, nobody tells the handler who sorted it, so we keep making the same call.
Customers phone to chase unsorted claims. We can't tell them anything, because the claim is waiting on their own documents.
We'd like auto-sorting so we can move three FTE onto complex claims.
Same customer, two claims in a month, and we didn't spot the first one when sorting the second. It should have been a closer look.
Can you add a "waiting for information" status? Unsorted mixes claims we haven't looked at with ones we can't sort yet.
Bulk select would save me so much time on the overnight glass claims.
Please confirm whether the predictive model you trialled with us in 2025 kept any decision records.
Our investigators want suspicious claims flagged earlier, before a handler has spent time on them.
Speed to payment is now one of our KPIs. Sorting is the first step, so anything that speeds it up.
Can the system auto-sort overnight claims so the morning shift starts with the piles ready?

RFP requirement 14: "AI-assisted triage, with an explainable reason recorded for every decision." Procurement asked in the Q&A round how decision records would be shown to their regulator. 
They saw the competitor's demo in August. Rep: "This is a must-have. They won't shortlist us without it. Every other requirement we're fine on.”

They promise customers payment within 24 hours on simple motor claims and miss it on about a fifth of claims (their figure, from the demo call). Their claims director said: 
“We want claims sorted the second they land.”
Rep: "Automatic sorting is the headline ask. I think what they actually care about is the 24-hour promise."

The ops director wants to cut handler headcount by 15% over two years. Automatic sorting came up as "how we get there”.
Rep: "They're a cost play. If we can show handler hours saved, the sorting question goes away."

They ticked "automatic sorting" as required on a 60-item requirements checklist. It didn't come up in either demo.
Rep: "Honestly not sure it matters to them. But it's a red cell on the scoresheet.”

They asked whether we can sort the easy claims in bulk. When I said bulk sorting ships in about six weeks, they were positive, but the head of claims said: "Bulk is nice. Automatic is what the board asked about."
Rep: "Bulk might be enough for the users. Not sure it's enough for the buyer."

They raised the competitor's pricing first, then automatic sorting. About 40 handlers.
Rep: "Price-led. Sorting feels like a reason to say no rather than a reason to say yes."

Quarterly review, 29 Sep 2026. Attended by their ops director and head of claims.

- Ops director: "Our board wants to see automation this year. The backlogs after the storms were embarrassing."
- Head of claims: "My handlers are drowning on Mondays and after any weather event."
- They asked when automatic sorting will be available, and whether they'd get it before renewal.
They mentioned that the competitor approached them in the summer.

CSM: "At risk. The ask is automatic sorting, but every example they gave was a volume spike.”

Annual review, 2 Oct 2026. Attended by their head of claims and compliance officer.

- Head of claims asked for automatic sorting and referred to the competitor's launch.
- The compliance officer then said: "Nothing goes live that we can't explain to the regulator, line by line."
- Their auditor raised a finding this year that sorting decisions have no recorded reason.
They asked what happened to the predictive model trialled with them in 2025.

CSM: "They want it and fear it in equal measure. Compliance has a veto."

Quarterly review, 14 Oct 2026. Attended by their ops manager and head of investigations.

- Ops manager asked for automatic sorting "to stop new starters sending everything to suspicious".
- Head of investigations said their team is spending time rejecting referrals that were never suspicious.
- Supervisor sign-off on the suspicious pile was described as "the bottleneck nobody owns".

CSM: "The pain is in the suspicious pile, not in sorting as a whole."
